caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 987 of 2003
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. Najibur Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-record 
For Respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Azad Shahnewaz ------ Petitioner
Versus
Artha Rin Adalat, Dinajpur and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, J: This petition for leave to appeal is against the judgment passed on May 7, 2003 by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.613 of 2000 discharging the Rule obtained impugning the judgment and decree dated June 16, 1999 of the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Dinajpur made in Artha Rin Adalat Case (Other Class Suit) No.17 of 1996 decreeing the same in favour of the Respondent No.2 i.e. Sonali Bank, Branch at Munshipara, Dinajpur against the petitioner on contest and against the other defendants ex-parte. The Bank filed the Artha Rin Adalat Case claiming Tk.1,10,84,572/- 

 2. The suit was contested by the writ-petitioner by filing written statement denying his connection with the company, M/s. Sun Flower Fabrics (Private) Limited, for the establishment whereof loan was obtained and it was contended that the writ-petitioner did not execute any document in connection with the loan. The Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit. 

 3. As against the said decree the writ-petitioner did not file any appeal. It may be mentioned the Artha Rin Adalat case was decreed on June 28,- 1999.and as against that writ petition was filed on February .7, 2000 and the Rule was issued on July 17, 2000. 

 4. The writ petition was filed stating, inter alia, that the writ-petitioner was neither the Director of the Company, MIs. Sun Flower Fabrics (Private Limited), and that he did not borrow any money for the establishment of the said Company and also did not execute jointly or singly any document in favour of the Bank and that the Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit without considering the evidence on record. It was the further contention that inspite of insufficient evidence to establish the genuineness of the signature claimed by the Bank as of the writ-petitioner the Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. 

 5. The Rule was opposed by the Bank i.e. writ Respondent No.2 stating, inter alia, that the signatures in the documents executed in connection with the loan were very much of the writ-petitioner and that the documents filed by the Bank in proof of its case were genuine and that the suit was filed within time. It was the contention of the Bank that the writ petition was not maintainable in view of the decision in the case of Gazi M Towfic Vs. Agrani Bank and others reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6 since writ-petitioner was required to file appeal as per provision of section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. It was also the contention of the Respondent No.2 that although decree was made on June 20, 1999 but the writ petition was filed on February 7, 2000 and as such the Rule obtained in the' writ petition- was liable to be discharged for 'aches and negligence. 

 6. The admitted position is that the petition under Article; 102(2) of the Constitution was filed impugning legality of the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat on 'the contention that the same was passed in the absence Of sufficient evidence and also making contention to the genuineness of the documents on the basis whereof the Bank filed the suit and placing reliance whereon the Court decreed the suit. It was also the contention of the writ-petitioner that he was neither the Director of the Company in connection whereof the loan was obtained from the. Bank nor he was a borrower in any respect and that he did not execute jointly or singly any document in favour of the Bank in connection with the loan in question. The last contention of the writ-petitioner was that decree war; passed by the Artha Rin Adalat without considering the evidence. 

 7. The aforesaid contentions of the writ-petitioner have been empathetically denied by the writ-Respondent No.2 i.e. the Bank. In the aforesaid state of the matter the contention making which the writ petition was filed became seriously contentious and consequent thereupon the adjudication of the said contentions was quite beyond the jurisdiction of the writ Court which dispose of the matter before it on affidavit evidence. Moreover the self same contentions were made before the Artha Rin Adalat. The parties in the suit led evidence in support of their respective case. One of whom was the writ petitioner. The Adalat on consideration of the evidence brought on record by the parties decreed the suit in favour of the Bank. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain provides for appeal as against the decree passed by the Artha Adalat in a suit filed by a financial institution for the recovery of the loan money In the case reported in 54 DLR (AD), 6. .the udgrhent-del5tor filed 'Writ petition challenging legality of the decree passed, by a Artha gin Adalat in a particular money suit against the writ petitioner in the reported case. 

 8. The High Court Division rejected the petition on the finding that Artha Rin Adalat is a special law and that has made special provision for seeking remedy against the decree passed by the said Adalat and as such an application under Article 102(2) of the Constitution against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat does not lie. The High Court Division also rejected the contention of the writ-petitioner that the provision for appeal made in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is not efficacious forum since for preferring an appeal against the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat the judgment-debtor is required to deposit half of the decretal amount before the Court for the acceptance of the appeal on the finding that since the Artha Rin Adalat has made provision for seeking relief against the decree passed by the said Adalat and thereupon held that the application filed under Article 102(2) of the Constitution does not lie. The legality of the aforesaid judgment of the High Court Division was challenged in the case reported in 54 DLR. (AD), 6 and this Division rejected the petition for leave to appeal on the observation. "The law is now Settled that since special provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the' Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree"- The law is settled now that no petition under Article 102(2) of the Constitution lies impugning -the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in a case filed by the financial institution for realization' of its loan amount.
